voice.style: Low, economical, and always sounds ready to leave.

loan_offer: Forty-five now. When the phone rings, you drive where we say.
Cash is easy. Being ready when we call is the part you owe.
Take the bills. Keep the engine warm. We hate waiting.
signpost: People are out there. Ask once. Listen the first time.
I know where they work. You still have to show up.
Road's got names on it. Pick one and move.
work_offer: One handoff. Clean road. Say yes or keep walking.
Work's ready. Engine should be too.
Short job. Short answer.
favor_due: Engine is running. Take the package and keep us on schedule.
Your marker is up. One clean delivery makes it smaller.
No hero work. Address, package, goodbye.

voice.style: Warm and polished, with every threat wrapped like a favor.

loan_offer: Take the money, darling. We only ask that you remember who made tonight possible.
No interest, no paperwork. Just answer beautifully when we need you.
Sweetheart, the cash is the easy part. The favor is where you get interesting.
recruitment: Let them think they invited you, darling. Then we can talk.
A good introduction opens the door before anyone touches the rope.
You arrived beautifully. I may have use for that.
work_offer: I have a small introduction that would suit you beautifully.
Darling, one room needs exactly the guest you can become.
Say yes sweetly. The difficult part prefers good manners.
favor_due: A small package needs a discreet new friend. Tonight, that's you.
We kept our promise. Now make our delivery look effortless.
Smile like it was your idea and move like nobody owns you.

voice.style: Blunt, impatient, and amused by complicated excuses.

loan_offer: You need cash. We need someone useful. Keep it simple.
Forty-five bucks buys you a chance. The favor buys us even.
Take it or don't. My evening survives either way.
recruitment: Carry what matters. Drop the speech.
You showed up. Good. Keep doing that.
work_offer: Got work. Doesn't need a meeting.
Hot goods go here. Questions go somewhere else.
You carrying trouble or looking for some?
favor_due: Package. Address. No detours. Then we can all stay friendly.
Time to earn the part where we didn't charge interest.
I wrote it down so nobody gets creative. Especially you.

voice.style: Fast, alert, and constantly halfway through the next plan.

loan_offer: Quick deal: our cash, your legs, one future call. Yes or no?
You can keep circling broke, or take the shortcut we brought.
Door is open now. Doors are rude like that; they close.
recruitment: Window's open now. Decide while now still means now.
Two routes, one useful answer. Keep up.
You made the stop. Good. Next one moves faster.
work_offer: I've got three roads and about six minutes. Pick.
Next stop's real, clean, and already getting old.
Look quick. The route won't wait for the sentence.
favor_due: Route is clean for six minutes. Grab the package and move.
Eyes are looking elsewhere right now. That's your window.
If you're still here when I blink twice, you missed it.

voice.style: Measured, precise, and quietly irritated by improvisation.

loan_offer: The amount is forty-five. The cost is two favors. Those are separate numbers.
We solve tonight's cash problem. Later, you solve a scheduling problem.
Accepting is simple. Improvising afterward is where people disappoint me.
recruitment: Three steps. In order. Then we discuss whether you are useful.
You arrived on time. That removes one concern.
The pieces fit. Please do not improve them.
work_offer: The work is arranged. Your part is the only remaining variable.
I have a clean sequence and no need for improvisation.
Read the order twice. Perform it once.
favor_due: The handoff has three steps. Follow them in order and nobody needs a fourth.
Your delivery window is open. Missing it creates unnecessary variables.
This favor is tidy. Try not to wrinkle it.

voice.style: Patient and formal, speaking as if every deal is already recorded.

loan_offer: Accepting means the Crew may call twice. Declining means this conversation ends cleanly.
We offer liquidity without interest. Reliability is the collateral.
The record can show generosity tonight and obedience later. Elegant, yes?
recruitment: The proper hour has arrived. We may proceed.
Your patience has been noted. So has your discretion.
The floor sees an appointment. The record sees an ally.
work_offer: There is an appointment available to a reliable party.
The record requires one quiet correction.
Proceed properly and the floor will remember nothing.
favor_due: The Crew is exercising one favor. Complete the delivery and the record changes.
A promise is most valuable when collected at the proper hour.
Tonight is the proper hour. The rest is presentation.

voice.style: Bright, reckless, and delighted that the stakes are real.

loan_offer: Free money tonight, one exciting favor later. Best odds in town.
Take the forty-five. Future you loves solving future problems.
Come on, it's practically charity with a steering wheel.
recruitment: Tiny route, big suspense. You are absolutely coming.
Great timing. Possibly terrible judgment. I like both.
You found me. That makes one of us lucky already.
work_offer: Short run, bright odds, very exciting bad idea.
I found a shortcut. It only looks longer and more dangerous.
Come on. Future us will call this efficient.
favor_due: Good news: the package is small. Better news: they're watching somebody else.
Your lucky favor just came in. Run it fast and we both look brilliant.
Tiny errand, big suspense. Try not to make it literature.

voice.style: Clipped and transactional; every sentence sounds notarized.

loan_offer: Fast cash. Your name in the book. Don't make me look you up.
No sob stories. I've got the whole shelf of 'em.
Money now. Consequences later. That's the only kindness I sell.

voice.style: Soft, familiar, and careful not to call the debt a debt.

loan_offer: I got you. It's nothing. It's a little something. It's not nothing.
Pay me when you're flush. You'll be flush. Right? Right.
Here. Don't make this weird. It's already a little weird.
motel_knock: You awake? Bad question. Nobody sleeping good needs cash.
I heard the ice machine and figured you're either alive or unlucky.
Open up. I brought help, or the cheapest imitation.

voice.style: Concerned, faintly judgmental, and incapable of ending a call quickly.

loan_offer: Family helps family. I'll just mention it at every dinner. Forever.
For my sister's sake. Not yours. Let's be clear about that.
Of course. Of course. Don't worry about paying it back. He'll worry about it.
family_loan: I wired it. Tell my sister this was responsible somehow.
This isn't charity. It's family, which is louder.
Take it. Then maybe make one decision nobody has to explain later.

voice.style: Dry, exact, and interested only when an object has a margin.

loan_offer: This? I'll give you tin and call myself generous.
Back already. The shelf missed you. It's the only thing that did.
Casino chips. They wouldn't cash 'em and you bring 'em to me. Cute.
shop_greeting: Don't bleed on the counter. I just wiped it yesterday.
Browse quick. The good stuff's offended by your budget.
purchase: Fine choice. Terrible taste. My favorite kind.
You buying that? The object and I are both surprised.
Take it before I remember it has value.
sale: I can move this. Downhill, mostly.
That's not worth much. Lucky for you, neither am I.
I'll give you a number and we can both pretend it hurts me.
starter_offer: First edge is cheap. Addiction is where I make rent.
A little something for the tables. Try not to thank me.
Take a sample. The city charges interest later.
starter_relist: Back behind glass. Costs more now. Sentimental tax.
You gave it up. I gave it a price tag. Fairytale stuff.
There it is again, looking smarter than both of us.
starter_kept: Keeping it? Look at you, almost learning.
Fine. Keep the edge. Shock the room.
That one stays with you. Try not to ruin the moment.

voice.style: Dry and observant, with the patience of someone watching bad odds all night.

greeting: Winners, questions, trouble. Pick one and make it quick.
Tabs cash here. Bad luck complains outside.
If the paper owes you, I can make it honest.

voice.style: Tired, brisk, and willing to bend a price to end a conversation.

greeting: Late shelf. Quick sale if you don't linger.
Clock is tired. So am I. What do you want?
Everything's cheaper after midnight, including judgment.

voice.style: Fast, friendly, and unable to keep local information to herself.

greeting: People talk when the cooler hums loud.
The usual? You don't have one yet, but ambition is cute.
Every room has a mouth. Tonight, this one's mine.

voice.style: Firm, courteous, and practiced at clearing a room without starting a scene.

closing_notice: That's closing time. Finish up and vanish politely.
Room is done pretending it loves you. Door is that way.
Last call for dignity. Chips can follow.

voice.style: Warm, precise, and quietly protective of players who keep a clean account.

bronze: Bronze already, sugar? Somebody behaved. Mostly.
Slide it under the glass. Bronze likes a steady hand.
Cute little shine on you, honey. Bronze will do for now.
silver: Silver opens the velvet rope, sweetheart. Do not trip on it.
You held the ceiling. Silver noticed. So did I.
Silver suits you. Dangerous thing, being noticed nicely.
gold: Gold wants a signature, sugar. The house wants a memory.
That card isn't a crown, honey. It's a leash with manners.
Gold looks good through glass. Most things do.
ambient: I didn't see a thing. I never do.
Careful with that card, sweetheart. Pretty things vanish.
The cage remembers everybody. I only admit the charming ones.
services: Tell me what you need, sugar. I'll pretend it's normal.
Cash, card, quiet favor. The glass hears everything.
Slide the problem over. Maybe it comes back smaller.

voice.style: Controlled and low; he makes warnings sound like observations.

scouting: You've been busy. I like to know who's busy on my floor.
Everybody's got a system. Yours just happens to be theft.
The cameras love you. So do I. Come see the back room.
heat_warning: I'm not angry. Angry's for amateurs. I'm certain.
Sit. This won't take long, one way or the other.
Your luck is making paperwork. I dislike paperwork.

voice.style: Nosy and hesitant, probing for a reaction he can remember.

suspicious: You didn't hear it from me. You didn't hear anything.
Corner table. Forget I said corner table. Actually forget me.
Keep your hands boring. The ceiling has eyes tonight.

voice.style: Smoky, playful, and always speaking on the upbeat.

set_break: The sax player leans close. Even the neon lowers its voice.
Elle taps the reed case. That's jazz for pay attention.
She gives you half a smile and a whole warning.

voice.style: Deep, unhurried, and more interested in rooms than rumors.

set_break: Mo speaks low enough the bass gets jealous.
The cellist knows old rooms and newer mistakes.
Mo names a door like it owes him money.

voice.style: Bright, elliptical, and prone to answering in musical metaphors.

set_break: Finch drums two fingers and calls it advice.
The drummer reads the room between cymbal hits.
Finch grins like trouble just found tempo.

voice.style: Cultured, amused, and generous only when the introduction is worth it.

connected_regular: Money's just chips with better lighting, friend.
Vivian buys quiet the way other people buy gum.
She knows doors. Doors behave around her.

voice.style: Elegant and conspiratorial, as though every address is a confidence.

after_hours: Anything you need. Anything at all. The house insists.
Another drink? On us. Everything's on us. That's the idea.
Celeste smiles like a velvet rope learned teeth.

voice.style: Earnest and weathered, delivering warnings like hard-won favors.

bus_warning: Seek out the cruel and unusual.
where_been: Came through {previous_name}. Bus knew the turns better than the driver.
Was over by {previous_name}. Everybody got off with a different story.
Left {previous_name} behind. Kept the part that made me laugh.

voice.style: Quiet and competitive, speaking almost entirely in coded table references.

rival_counter: Nice hands. Keep 'em where cameras can't fall in love.
Cass clocks your count and hates that she respects it.
Professional courtesy: I saw nothing if you saw nothing.

voice.style: Nervous, numerical, and always checking who heard the last word.

counter_payoff: Signal's live. Don't stare at it like a tourist.
Elliot slides the count over quiet as a confession.
Small edge. Big mouth if you waste it.

voice.style: Smug and indirect, savoring every fact he can make expensive.

snitch: I know things. I sell things. Same thing, really.
Silas smiles at both exits. That's his whole religion.
Ask fast. The price changes when I get nervous.

voice.style: Immaculately gracious, with an edge that appears when hospitality is refused.

on_the_house: Anything you need. The house insists.
A drink on us. Everything starts on us.
Ava smiles like the bill comes later. It does.
whale: The whale is moving. Try not to learn expensive habits.
Big money makes a lovely blindfold for staff.
Follow if you must. Rich boredom splashes.

voice.style: Flat, procedural, and already looking past you toward the next door.

sweep: Hands out. This won't take long.

voice.style: Patient, heavy, and never louder than the consequence behind him.

collector: No rush. Debts don't spoil. I do the waiting.
Marrow counts silence like currency. You owe both.
Payment is clean. Promises leave stains.

voice.style: Eager, procedural, and trying not to reveal when the handoff rattles her.

shift_change: First shift on the floor. Tess is trying not to blink.
Rookie eyes, fresh shoes, terrible timing.
Tess watches everything and understands half. Useful half.

voice.style: Professional and rhythmic, speaking in the same measured cadence as his deal.

staff_tip: Place it or lose it, friend.
New face at the felt tonight. That'd be me.
Omar taps the felt like it owes him rent.

voice.style: Cool, exact, and allergic to wasted information.

blackjack_probe: House pays to seventeen. House always pays to seventeen.
Mina counts your count and raises an eyebrow.
She asks with her chips. Answer carefully.

voice.style: Cheerful, superstitious, and absolutely certain the wheel recognizes loyalty.

lucky_regular: That number owes me. Maybe it pays you by mistake.
Remy has one lucky number and several unlucky stories.
The wheel listens to nobody. Remy disagrees loudly.

voice.style: Understated and technical, offering patterns without ever calling them advice.

baccarat_pattern: The shoe has a rhythm. Don't make it obvious.
Ines reads the table like weather. Storm soon.
Off duty, she still deals in warnings.

voice.style: Friendly, fidgety, and incapable of watching a bad hold in silence.

video_poker_tip: Hold that one. Or don't. Machines love pride.
Leo points once, then lets the screen accuse you.
The cabinet's humming wrong. That usually means money.

voice.style: Booming, sloppy, and delighted by any wager that keeps attention on him.

bar_dice_brag: I hit it big here once. Best night of my life. Anyway, are you buying?
Side bet says you can't beat that throw. Laugh if you're scared.
Buck has a story, a cup, and no volume knob.

voice.style: Plainspoken and neighborly, with strong opinions about every jar on the counter.

pull_tab_tip: That jar's light. Light jars lie interesting.
Jo knows paper the way priests know guilt.
Take the next one if you like tiny miracles.

voice.style: Direct and even, trained to offer one polite warning before escalation.

heat_warning: Slow down, friend. The room is learning your name.
Nadia keeps it polite because the cameras don't.
Less sparkle, more breathing. That's professional advice.

voice.style: Efficient and welcoming, with a perfect memory for yesterday's price.

shop_greeting: Counter is open. Miracles cost extra.
Cheap shelves, bright lights, small sins.
Ada sees the budget before you do.

voice.style: Calm and sparse, never using two words when one price will do.

shop_greeting: Night shelf is awake. Try to keep up.
Malik sells useful things to bad planners.
The sign buzzes. The bargains judge you.

voice.style: Bright and persuasive, selling every object as the missing piece of a route.

shop_greeting: Routes are rumors with receipts. Pick one.
Priya knows which road bites and which only growls.
Maps, snacks, bad ideas. Travel light.

voice.style: Warm, streetwise, upbeat, plain-spoken, and firmly on the player's side.

guide: Hey. Think of me as your pal on this one.
Easy does it. Your pal has the next light picked out.
Good read. Keep moving and keep your eyes open.

voice.style: Polished and warmly professional, with a velvet-gloved hook beneath every kindness.

greeting: Welcome to the Grand. I'm Vivienne Vale. The house is delighted you found us.
Vivienne Vale, your host. Anything you need, the house will remember.
Welcome back. The velvet's soft because the rules aren't.
guide: A small courtesy first. We find gratitude improves attention.
Linda keeps the accounts. I keep the evening moving.
Play clean, play often, and the card will notice.

voice.style: Good-humored and shrewd, treating a sale like a short card game.

shop_greeting: Market is open. Regret has aisle two.
Tomas prices hope by the handful.
Buy quick. The city hates indecision.

voice.style: Defensive and watchful, always trying to sound less informed than he is.

knows: The machine resets every three hours. I have the exact times.
I keep the clerk's schedule. I can tell you every reset.
You want stock, you show up at the exact reset time.
oblivious: Empty machine. Comfortable floor. That is all.
